status.en: 24 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 33% fewer than the week before, most of them in Tigray, Amhara and Addis Ababa.
status.nb: 24 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 33 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Tigray, Amhara og Addis Ababa.

summary.en: Ethiopian federal forces have seized the strategic Tigray town of Adwa and its airport near the Eritrean border, while a pro-government militia also reports taking the airport. Ethiopian drones have struck Eritrean troops that entered Ethiopian territory to support Tigrayan rebels, and heavy weapons are being moved toward the Eritrean border. The United Nations has allocated $8.5 million for humanitarian response as the conflict escalates in northern Ethiopia. Ethiopia and Somaliland are discussing defense cooperation. The war caused 2,824 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Etiopiske føderale styrker har tatt den strategiske Tigray-byen Adwa og flyplassen der, nær grensen mot Eritrea, mens en pro-regjeringsmilits også melder at de har tatt flyplassen. Etiopiske droner har angrepet eritreiske tropper som gikk inn i etiopisk territorium for å støtte tigrayanske opprørere, og tunge våpen blir flyttet mot grensen mot Eritrea. FN har avsatt 8.5 millioner dollar til humanitært svar etter hvert som konflikten eskalerer i Nord-Etiopia. Etiopia og Somaliland diskuterer forsvarssamarbeid. Krigen forårsaket 2 824 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Fano insurgency
background.extract: The Fano insurgency is an armed conflict and insurgency in the Amhara Region of Ethiopia that began in April 2023 between the Fano militia and the Ethiopian government. The conflict started after the government attempted to dissolve the Amhara Special Forces and other regional forces as part of a plan to reform and centralize the country's security apparatus, and integrate them into the federal armed forces. This move led to protests and armed resistance by local forces under Fano.
